title: Munkhbat Charles Batsaikhan
text:
I’m a data scientist and Statistics major at Macalester (’25). Right now I’m a Data Scientist Intern with Metro Transit’s Data & Business group, where I handle customer-facing issues and work with planners, field operations, and other stakeholders to turn data into useful answers. I build reproducible pipelines, sanity checks, and interactive dashboards that help track stop and route performance and the rider experience. I use R, SQL, Python (with Shiny, Quarto), and I like translating what stakeholders need into clear metrics and actions. I care about careful methods and practical results—especially when they make public services run better.

title: Analyzing the Opioid Epidemic
text:
Introduction
In this project, my group mates and I delve into the critical issue of the opioid epidemic, employing data analysis techniques and interactive visualizations to understand its impact and identify potential patterns.

title: Analyzing the Opioid Epidemic
text:
Objectives

Data Exploration: Dive into datasets related to opioid usage, overdose incidents, and associated factors.
Trend Analysis: Identify temporal trends and geographical patterns to better comprehend the evolution of the epidemic.
Interactive Visualizations: Utilize R and RShiny to create dynamic visualizations for enhanced data exploration.

title: Analyzing the Opioid Epidemic
text:
Methodology
I approach the analysis with a combination of statistical methods and data visualization tools. Leveraging the power of R and RShiny, I aim to provide an insightful perspective on the opioid epidemic.

title: Analyzing the Opioid Epidemic
text:
Expected Outcomes
Through this project, I anticipate shedding light on the opioid epidemic’s dynamics, contributing valuable insights that may inform future interventions and policies.

Thanks for stopping by!
I’m a Data Scientist Intern at Metro Transit (Metropolitan Council).
My interests include causal inference, geospatial analysis, and transit analytics. I like building clean, reproducible pipelines in R/Python and turning them into useful visualizations and apps.

text:
About me


Stats major with a focus on data for public good.
I work mostly in R (tidyverse, sf, Shiny) and SQL, with growing Python usage. I care about explainability, data ethics, and shipping tools that real people actually use. You’ll often find me iterating in Quarto and Shiny.


Transit analytics & GTFS/RT data pipelines


Urban climate & environmental equity (LST, tree canopy, SVI)


Causal graphs, matching, and sensitivity analysis




Before Metro Transit, I researched environmental inequality in Minneapolis, combining historical housing data with modern climate and health indicators. I enjoy mapping, teaching stats concepts, and building dashboards that make complex analyses easy to explore.
